question: Which upstream factor actually produces repeated value preference for negative progress?
resource: Local RTX3060 and CPU only. No external parent, recovery controller or Bayesian experiment.

baseline.policy: Frozen seed61 GRU, corrected canonical terminal score, original safety/smoothing/reward/humans/time limit

three_level_contrast.source: Fixed historical states, replayed recorded prefix; score and all continuations use repaired frozen GRU. Separately mark states no longer visited by repaired baseline.
three_level_contrast.actions: Current repaired selected action versus maximum goal progress among the same safe executable candidates
three_level_contrast.A: CV-predicted successor value and corrected immediate task Q; retain risk/tie components separately
three_level_contrast.B: Actual one-step successor observation and updated legal history, same frozen network; true native immediate reward and terminal masking
three_level_contrast.C: Execute each fixed first action then identical repaired GRU until native termination, same physical state, human future and remaining time

upstream_contrasts.condition: Only run contrasts that distinguish the A/B/C result; each changes one factor and preserves the first forced action
allowed: future exploration0 versus.05 with common indexed draws
upstream_contrasts.selection: All 164 fixed roots including original successes, not failures only
upstream_contrasts.long_human_tape: Generate with unchanged official pedestrian code and verify every existing saved prefix before use. Save separately.
upstream_contrasts.interpretation: Counterfactual contract effects are not automatically causes of training weights; isolate learning with a matched targeted training only if required.

training_allowance.maximum: One selected causal factor, intervention plus matched control
training_allowance.budget: Reuse identical frozen IL checkpoint; <=2000 RL episodes per arm, seed61, all non-target parameters matched
training_allowance.freeze_before_outcomes: Separate causal-training protocol and commit required after A/B/C identifies the factor

decision_rules.successor_model: A/B ranking reversal plus actual C correction supports a prediction-induced error, not merely changed features; quantify fields and affected episodes.
decision_rules.value_error: B ranks the selected action higher while C favors the forward action: realized policy-continuation ranking error. Distinguish task-clock mismatch from other learning/distribution error.
decision_rules.policy_limitation: A/B/C agree but a saved alternative continuation succeeds safely: frozen policy continuation limitation, not automatically critic misranking.
decision_rules.causal_factor: Source evidence plus one-factor intervention changes the predicted mechanism and actual failures, includes normal successes and counterexamples. Report coverage, not universal claims.
decision_rules.go: Proceed only with a specific upstream factor's discriminating causal test; no new algorithm development.
decision_rules.kill: Stop a causal explanation if its predicted ranking/outcome effect is absent; do not add arbitrary factors or tune parameters.
decision_rules.unresolved: If explanations remain inseparable, preserve exact evidence and one discriminating follow-up experiment; do not manufacture a unique root cause.

preflight: Check repaired helper equals canonical policy selection, action support80, tape and executed positions, two deterministic repetitions and actual successor construction before full cohort.
accounting: Native outcome and independent swept geometry separately; episode/case-level summaries, no independent-root inference; single training seed.
